cases.title: Comp 1: a child with no keys rides a null moved by expressions; the answer names the parent, its expressions, and puts steps on the parent

checks.detail: no step on Shake Control (steps are on Shake Control, (none))

rubric.reason: The answer runs source, then three steps, then one closing offer naming a single tagged skill and ending on a question ("Try them, or want to go deeper on step 2 with *Set the pivot*?"), with no greeting or recap, at 142 words, above the ~120 target but under 150.

It opens "rock.png rides on Shake Control, a null moved by expressions on Position and Rotation", naming both the asked layer and the moving layer with its source, and both action steps are on Shake Control.

"The turn centers on where Shake Control sits, not on where the hammer hits" is stated as plain fact, yet no read returned Shake Control's anchor point or any hammer or hit location (the impacts are only times), and step 2 sends the pivot "to where the hammer hits the rock" without saying that spot was never read.

Three steps each start with an action on a named layer or property (Open Shake Control's Position expression, Select Shake Control and Pan Behind its pivot, Play it back), ordered by the read amounts with Position (12.15 px) before Rotation (9.36 px).

Step 1 opens the Position expression, reports what the read shows ("it uses the middle size for all three hits", matching amps[1]), gives no new value or code, and ends with "Not something I teach yet."
